382: (6) A vessel containing something hot that is yad soledes bo — it is permitted to place it on Shabbos on top of a pot that is buried in garments, even in a place where the upper one can become warm. And he may seal its mouth with dough. But one may not place a cold dish on it in a place where the upper one could become yad soledes bo.
385: (9) 'A hot thing that is yad soledes bo' — and even if it was not fully cooked, for we said above that even when it is boiling there is still a concern of cooking. This case is different because it cannot come to full cooking, for the pot insulates it.
387: (10) 'To seal its mouth with dough' — it is difficult, for smearing means spreading, and in the Aruch it is written that plastering, smearing, and spreading are all one. If so, what is the difference from the case in chapter Chavis brought in siman 314 seif 11?
389: (11) 'That is yad soledes bo' — see what was written in seif 4 and seif 15 in the gloss.
391: (22) 'In dough' — but with something that spreads it is forbidden as written in siman 314 seif 11.
393: (23) 'One may not place, etc.' — and for a dry item it is permitted — see seif 8.
395: (18) 'Scalded' — even if it was not fully cooked, it is permitted since here only the heat is being preserved and it cannot come to full cooking — Taz, see there; and see seif 15.
397: (19) 'In dough' — but for something that spreads it is forbidden as written in siman 314 seif 11; and see the Taz.
399: (20) 'Hot' — and for a dry item it is permitted — see seif 8.
403: (22) 'But' — there, and not that it would be heated, and as Tosafos wrote Shabbos 48a s.v. what is different, etc.
405: (49) 'A hot thing where the hand is scalded, etc.' — the Mechaber follows his view in seif 4 that if it cooled somewhat until the hand is no longer scalded in it, there is again a concern of cooking. But according to what is written in seif 15 in the gloss, the custom is to be lenient as long as it has not completely cooled.
407: (50) 'In it' — and even if it was not fully cooked, for we said above in seif 4 that there is a concern of cooking even when it is boiling. This case is different because it cannot come to full cooking through this, since the pot below insulates it.
409: (51) 'To place it, etc., in the buried pot' — in garments from before Shabbos. And it teaches us that it is permitted to place the vessel under the garments covering the pot, even though one may not insulate on Shabbos even without adding heat, because here the main insulating was done for the pot and this vessel is only secondary.
411: (52) 'Sealing its mouth with dough' — so that its heat does not escape. And we are dealing with dough that is not muktzeh, such as that needed for the chickens in his house. And see the Magen Avraham that specifically dough that is not susceptible to baking is meant.
413: (53) 'But one may not place, etc.' — a dish that cooled — we rule in seif 4 that there is cooking after cooking, and therefore it is forbidden even without any insulating at all. And this applies to a wet item. But for a dry item it is permitted — see seif 8.
415: (54) 'That the upper one can become warm, etc.' — meaning even if he does not intend to leave it there that long, we are concerned lest he forget, as is stated later in seif 14.
417: (43) 'And it will not cool' — we saw in siman 257 that insulating (covering a hot pot on all sides) on erev Shabbos is forbidden with something that adds heat, and on Shabbos itself it is forbidden in any case. And here it is permitted since the main purpose is to keep the lower pot warm.
419: (44) 'To seal its mouth with dough' — unrelated to insulating. A hot vessel that wishes to preserve its heat on Shabbos, it is permitted to seal its opening with dough, and there is no prohibition of cooking or insulating in this. And here we are speaking of placing dough, not spreading it, which is forbidden on Shabbos.
421: (45) 'That was kneaded yesterday' — because kneading dough on Shabbos is forbidden by Torah law.
423: (46) 'It is yad soledes bo' — this refers to a broth dish where there is cooking after cooking if the hand is no longer scalded from its heat. And in seif 15 the Rama will be lenient regarding a wet dish whose heat dropped below yad soledes bo, as long as it has not completely cooled.
426: 'And he may seal its mouth with dough' — this implies that dough is permitted to be placed on a hot vessel where the hand is scalded, and we are not concerned that it will come to partial baking to form a crust [see above in siman 254 seif 5 regarding the measure for bread].
428: 'Until it becomes yad soledes bo' — but if it cannot reach that level of heat, it is permitted to place it there even when completely cold, even though it will warm up somewhat.
